children.text: Use the following specified physical models. For laminar incompressible flow through a vessel of radius r and length ℓ, \(\Delta P=RQ\), \(R=8\eta\ell/(\pi r^4)\). A symmetric tree has N levels numbered 0 through N−1. Each vessel splits into two, with \(r_{i+1}=r_i/2^{1/3}\), \(\ell_{i+1}=\ell_i/2^{1/3}\). The pressure drop across the whole tree is ΔP. Use 760 mmHg=\(1.013\times10^{5}\) Pa. The elastic-vessel equivalent circuit is a series R,L feeding a shunt C, with outlet pressure across C, \(C=3\ell\pi r^3/(2Eh)\), \(L=9\ell\rho/(4\pi r^2)\). Here E is wall Young modulus and h its thickness. The numerical tree has N=6, r0=\(6.0\times10^{-5}\) m, ℓ0=\(2.0\times10^{-3}\) m, inlet pressure 55 mmHg, capillary pressure 30 mmHg, η=\(3.5\times10^{-3}\) kg/(m s), ρ=\(1.05\times10^{3}\) kg/m³, E=0.06 MPa.

Assuming the same h at every level, estimate its maximum value for attenuation throughout the numerical tree.

children.text: An inextensible sphere initially contains normal tissue of density ρ0. A central tumour grows, with fixed normal-tissue mass. The densities are ρN=ρ0(1+p/KN), ρT=ρ0(1+p/KT), with common excess pressure p. Define v=VT/V, μ=MT/MN, κ=KN/KT. Find v(μ,κ), selecting the physical branch.

A spherical tumour of radius RT generates uniform heating power density P. Tumour and all surrounding tissue have conductivity k. Temperature far away is Tb=310.15 K. Find the steady centre temperature.
For RT=5.0 cm and k=0.60 W/(m K), find the threshold power density to raise every tumour cell from 37°C to above 43°C.

Only level N−1 vessels narrow by positive δr. Their collapse law is \(p/P_{cap}-1=(p_c/P_{cap}-1)(2-\delta r/\delta r_c)\delta r/\delta r_c\). At fixed whole-tree pressure drop and small p−Pcap, find the signed relative flow change δQ/Q in terms of v,KN,N,pc,δrc,rN−1,Pcap.

statement.text:
Physics of Live Systems
Use the following specified physical models. For laminar incompressible flow through a vessel of radius r and length ℓ, \(\Delta P=RQ\), \(R=8\eta\ell/(\pi r^4)\). A symmetric tree has N levels numbered 0 through N−1. Each vessel splits into two, with \(r_{i+1}=r_i/2^{1/3}\), \(\ell_{i+1}=\ell_i/2^{1/3}\). The pressure drop across the whole tree is ΔP. Use 760 mmHg=\(1.013\times10^{5}\) Pa. The elastic-vessel equivalent circuit is a series R,L feeding a shunt C, with outlet pressure across C, \(C=3\ell\pi r^3/(2Eh)\), \(L=9\ell\rho/(4\pi r^2)\). Here E is wall Young modulus and h its thickness. The numerical tree has N=6, r0=\(6.0\times10^{-5}\) m, ℓ0=\(2.0\times10^{-3}\) m, inlet pressure 55 mmHg, capillary pressure 30 mmHg, η=\(3.5\times10^{-3}\) kg/(m s), ρ=\(1.05\times10^{3}\) kg/m³, E=0.06 MPa.

a.1. Flow in each generation
Find Qi in terms of ΔP,N,η,r0,ℓ0 and i.
a.2. Numerical inlet flow
Calculate Q0 in mL/hour.
a.3. Pressure amplitude transfer

For sinusoidal inlet pressure of angular frequency ω find Pout/Pin and the condition that low-frequency outlet oscillations are attenuated. Express the condition in η,ρ,E,h,r,ℓ.
a.4. Wall thickness bound
Assuming the same h at every level, estimate its maximum value for attenuation throughout the numerical tree.
b.1. Tumour volume fraction

An inextensible sphere initially contains normal tissue of density ρ0. A central tumour grows, with fixed normal-tissue mass. The densities are ρN=ρ0(1+p/KN), ρT=ρ0(1+p/KT), with common excess pressure p. Define v=VT/V, μ=MT/MN, κ=KN/KT. Find v(μ,κ), selecting the physical branch.
b.2. Central temperature
A spherical tumour of radius RT generates uniform heating power density P. Tumour and all surrounding tissue have conductivity k. Temperature far away is Tb=310.15 K. Find the steady centre temperature.
b.3. Heating all tumour cells
For RT=5.0 cm and k=0.60 W/(m K), find the threshold power density to raise every tumour cell from 37°C to above 43°C.
b.4. Flow reduction under compression
Only level N−1 vessels narrow by positive δr. Their collapse law is \(p/P_{cap}-1=(p_c/P_{cap}-1)(2-\delta r/\delta r_c)\delta r/\delta r_c\). At fixed whole-tree pressure drop and small p−Pcap, find the signed relative flow change δQ/Q in terms of v,KN,N,pc,δrc,rN−1,Pcap.

children.text: At level i, \(Q_i=Q_0/2^i\), while \(R_i=2^iR_0\). Each level therefore drops the same pressure Q0R0. Thus \[Q_i=\frac{\Delta P\pi r_0^4}{2^{i+3}N\ell_0\eta}.\]
Convert ΔP=25 mmHg to 3332 Pa. Then Q0≈\(4.04\times10^{-10}\) m³/s≈1.45 mL/hour, conventionally rounded to 1.5.

Complex impedances give \[\frac{P_{out}}{P_{in}}=\frac1{\sqrt{(1-\omega^2LC)^2+\omega^2C^2R^2}}.\] To quadratic order in ω, attenuation requires C²R²−2CL>0, or \(64\eta^2\ell^2/(3Ehr^3\rho)>1\). At equality attenuation first appears at fourth order.
The bound is \(h<64\eta^2\ell_i^2/(3Er_i^3\rho)=7.7\times10^{-5}2^{i/3}\,\mathrm m\). The strictest condition is at i=0, giving h less than about 77 μm.

Normal mass conservation gives p=KN v/(1−v). Eliminating p from the tumour mass relation yields \((1-\kappa)v^2-(1+\mu)v+\mu=0\). The branch tending to zero as μ→0 is \[v=\frac{1+\mu-\sqrt{(1+\mu)^2-4\mu(1-\kappa)}}{2(1-\kappa)}.\] At κ=1 the continuous limit is v=μ/(1+μ).
Conservation of heat gives \(T(r)-T_b=P R_T^3/(3kr)\) outside and \(T(r)-T_b=P R_T^2/(2k)-Pr^2/(6k)\) inside. Match temperature and heat flux at RT. At the centre \(T(0)=T_b+P R_T^2/(2k)\).

The coldest tumour point is its surface, not its centre. \(T(R_T)-T_b=PR_T^2/(3k)\). The threshold is \(P_{min}=3k(6\,\mathrm K)/R_T^2=4.32\,\mathrm{kW/m^3}\). Strictly exceeding 43°C requires power above this threshold.

Linearizing the collapse law gives \(\delta r=\delta r_c(p-P_{cap})/[2(p_c-P_{cap})]\). The last level's resistance increases by 4δr/r, while all N unperturbed levels contribute equally. Hence \[\frac{\delta Q}{Q}=-\frac{2}{N}\frac{K_Nv-(1-v)P_{cap}}{(1-v)(p_c-P_{cap})}\frac{\delta r_c}{r_{N-1}}.\] This applies on the narrowing side p>Pcap and is negative. Symmetry gives the same relative change in every level.

solution.text:
Physics of Live Systems
a.1. Flow in each generation
At level i, \(Q_i=Q_0/2^i\), while \(R_i=2^iR_0\). Each level therefore drops the same pressure Q0R0. Thus \[Q_i=\frac{\Delta P\pi r_0^4}{2^{i+3}N\ell_0\eta}.\]
a.2. Numerical inlet flow
Convert ΔP=25 mmHg to 3332 Pa. Then Q0≈\(4.04\times10^{-10}\) m³/s≈1.45 mL/hour, conventionally rounded to 1.5.
a.3. Pressure amplitude transfer
Complex impedances give \[\frac{P_{out}}{P_{in}}=\frac1{\sqrt{(1-\omega^2LC)^2+\omega^2C^2R^2}}.\] To quadratic order in ω, attenuation requires C²R²−2CL>0, or \(64\eta^2\ell^2/(3Ehr^3\rho)>1\). At equality attenuation first appears at fourth order.
a.4. Wall thickness bound
The bound is \(h<64\eta^2\ell_i^2/(3Er_i^3\rho)=7.7\times10^{-5}2^{i/3}\,\mathrm m\). The strictest condition is at i=0, giving h less than about 77 μm.
b.1. Tumour volume fraction
Normal mass conservation gives p=KN v/(1−v). Eliminating p from the tumour mass relation yields \((1-\kappa)v^2-(1+\mu)v+\mu=0\). The branch tending to zero as μ→0 is \[v=\frac{1+\mu-\sqrt{(1+\mu)^2-4\mu(1-\kappa)}}{2(1-\kappa)}.\] At κ=1 the continuous limit is v=μ/(1+μ).
b.2. Central temperature
Conservation of heat gives \(T(r)-T_b=P R_T^3/(3kr)\) outside and \(T(r)-T_b=P R_T^2/(2k)-Pr^2/(6k)\) inside. Match temperature and heat flux at RT. At the centre \(T(0)=T_b+P R_T^2/(2k)\).
b.3. Heating all tumour cells
The coldest tumour point is its surface, not its centre. \(T(R_T)-T_b=PR_T^2/(3k)\). The threshold is \(P_{min}=3k(6\,\mathrm K)/R_T^2=4.32\,\mathrm{kW/m^3}\). Strictly exceeding 43°C requires power above this threshold.
b.4. Flow reduction under compression
Linearizing the collapse law gives \(\delta r=\delta r_c(p-P_{cap})/[2(p_c-P_{cap})]\). The last level's resistance increases by 4δr/r, while all N unperturbed levels contribute equally. Hence \[\frac{\delta Q}{Q}=-\frac{2}{N}\frac{K_Nv-(1-v)P_{cap}}{(1-v)(p_c-P_{cap})}\frac{\delta r_c}{r_{N-1}}.\] This applies on the narrowing side p>Pcap and is negative. Symmetry gives the same relative change in every level.
